CHIEF COMPLAINT
Annual exam

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Andrea is a 52-year-old female with past medical history of rheumatoid arthritis, atrial fibrillation, and reflux presenting for her annual exam. She reports that she has been walking, exercising, and doing yoga as recommended, which has helped significantly with her arthritis. She denies any joint pain, stiffness, or flare-ups over the past year. She continues to take methotrexate once weekly without issues. Regarding her atrial fibrillation, she reports ongoing palpitations with the most recent episode approximately one week ago. She notes that palpitations tend to flare up with stress and has been attempting meditation and running with her dog to manage stress without significant relief. An event monitor was performed last month. Regarding her reflux, she reports that cutting out soda and taking protonix has helped significantly, and she has not had a flare-up in over five months.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient endorses palpitations and nasal congestion related to allergies. Denies chest pain, shortness of breath, nausea, or vomiting.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Rheumatoid arthritis
Atrial fibrillation
Reflux

MEDICATIONS
Methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly
Protonix 40 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient exercises regularly including walking, yoga, and running with her dog.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Heart rate well-controlled and regular. General: Heart rate nice and controlled. Cardiovascular: Slight 2/6 systolic ejection murmur appreciated, consistent with prior exams. Regular rate and rhythm at this time. Pulmonary: Lungs clear bilaterally. Extremities: Right elbow with edema and erythema, pain to palpation. No lower extremity edema.

RESULTS
Event monitor: Shows patient going in and out of atrial fibrillation with conversion pauses, characterized by periods of a-fib followed by pause then return to regular rhythm.
Autoimmune panel: All results within normal limits, indicating good control of rheumatoid arthritis on current methotrexate therapy.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Rheumatoid arthritis: Well-controlled on methotrexate. Continue methotrexate 2.5 mg once weekly. Refill ordered. Referral to rheumatology as needed.
2. Atrial fibrillation: Patient experiencing intermittent episodes. Refer to cardiology for cardiac ablation to map and ablate the source of the arrhythmia to maintain normal sinus rhythm.
3. Reflux: Well-controlled on protonix. Continue protonix 40 mg daily. Continue dietary modifications including avoiding coffee and spicy foods.
